items.title: IEEFA/JMK: India module capacity ~7x cell and ~116x ingot-wafer capacity; utilisation 35-40%
items.text: An IEEFA analysis modelled by JMK Research, reposted 23 Oct 2026, puts India's module capacity at about 233 GW by June 2026, roughly 7x cell capacity and 116x ingot-wafer capacity. Module makers run at about 35-40% utilisation versus the 50-65% needed for sustainable operations, with about 135 GW more module capacity firmly committed. It underlines the upstream gap that ALMM List-III is meant to close, but also the overcapacity risk for module-heavy listed makers.

items.title: JM Financial: China's proposed solar tech export curbs could speed India's wafer push
items.text: China's commerce and science ministries proposed on 16 Oct adding 12 solar PV manufacturing technologies (polysilicon, wafers, cells and related equipment) to its prohibited/restricted export catalogue; feedback is open until 15 Nov 2026. JM Financial called it structurally positive for Indian manufacturing and said the greatest opportunity lies upstream, but warned of near-term disruption since India depends on China for equipment, gases, chemicals and engineers. It added that India may relax the ALMM-II mandate beyond December 2026 if domestic prices rise sharply.

items.title: Agastya Energy CEO flags utilisation risk as India ingot-wafer capacity heads to ~80 GW
items.text: In a Mercom interview, Agastya Energy CEO Bernhard Rack said India's ingot and wafer capacity is projected at about 80 GW by June 2028 against ALMM List-III's 15 GW threshold. A 12 GW plant needs roughly 80-85% utilisation to be globally competitive; at 60%, fixed cost per watt is about 50% higher. He noted 200+ GW of module capacity runs at about 35-40% utilisation, a caution for listed names building multi-GW wafer plants.
